implementation_notes: Japan's comprehensive national 'AI Strategy 2022', decided by the Integrated Innovation Strategy Promotion Council on April 22, 2022 (Reiwa 4), expanding AI Strategy 2019 and 2021 in response to COVID-19, mega-disaster risks, climate departure, and geopolitical shifts (subsequently superseded by the December 2025 First AI Basic Plan). Structured in four parts: Part 1 establishes Strategic Goals 0–4 (imminent crisis resilience, AI talent, real-world industrial competitiveness, inclusive sustainable society, and global research/education networks); Part 2 details 'AI for National Resilience' (disaster/armed-attack Digital Twins, global BCP/data-economy networks), 'AI for Planetary Resilience' (Nature-Positive Economy), and 'Resilient and Responsible AI' (XAI, Federated Learning, Security for AI / AI for Security); Part 3 promotes social implementation (human-AI collaboration, breaking black-box fears, physical-cyber 'Round 2 of DX', data-handling rule reviews, government adoption, and focusing on Japanese strengths); Part 4 sets 2025 education targets (1M high school grads, 500k university/KOSEN grads, 250k applied AI talent, 2,000 experts, 1M working adults/yr recurrent education), R&D network restructuring, trust-data infrastructure, Digital Government AI guidelines, SME/startup support, and international ethics/standardization (GPAI presidency) avoiding excessive regulatory constraints.
